clue.text: Shout is aimed at nymph

parts.note: to shout is to call out
taken as written
something aimed at a target is directed to it

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a mythical nymph, the shout directed straight at her.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is a nymph of Greek myth, loved by Zeus and turned into a bear.

clue.text: Tacky East European replacing rings in particular

indicators.note: replacing means one pair of letters takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a particular person is fussy or choosy
rings are round, each like the letter O
E is east and E is European, giving two letters

explanation.surface: Someone fussy finds Eastern European jewellery tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing rings in' swaps the two Os of CHOOSY for E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy is informal for tacky, cheap and in poor taste.

clue.text: Not quite acceptable to eat hard fruit

indicators.note: to eat something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other
not quite means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: licit means lawful, acceptable
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hard fruit is not quite fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims LICIT to LICI; 'to eat' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichi, also spelt lychee, is a sweet Asian fruit.

clue.text: Old priest holding drug-smoking equipment lifts base

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters, so they are read from the bottom up
holding means the priest's name contains the other piece

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel
a bong is a water pipe for smoking drugs

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric caught with a drug pipe raises the moral tone, or lowers it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts BONG in ELI for ELBONGI; 'lifts' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low and dishonourable, a synonym of ignoble.

clue.text: Toddlers on view in time Harry succeeded

indicators.note: in means the first pair of pieces sits inside the next pair

parts.note: Harry is a pet form of the name Harold
re means on or concerning, as in letters
an eye is a view or way of seeing, as in 'in my eye'
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in family trees

explanation.surface: A small child appears in public just as Prince Harry comes into his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts REEYE inside T plus HAROLD, after the H; S closes it. Harry is a pet name for Harold as well as Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Children aged three are toddlers, just past babyhood.

clue.text: Edge of far continent invaded by cold band

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter here, the leading edge
the continent is entered by the cold letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Asia is a continent
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cold front sweeps into a distant continent, like a band of weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge of' takes F, the first letter of 'far'; 'invaded by' puts C inside ASIA to make ASCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is a flat band or strip, as in architecture or above a shopfront.

clue.text: Spray diseased oat, corn area being forgotten

indicators.note: diseased means unsound, so the letters are knocked out of shape
a letter being forgotten is left out of the word

parts.note: maize is corn

explanation.surface: Crops of oats and corn are sprayed because the plants are diseased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area being forgotten' takes A out of MAIZE for MIZE; 'diseased' rearranges OAT with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomize is to reduce a liquid to a fine spray.

clue.text: Associate of a university in different parts of school

indicators.note: in means the letter A is placed inside the school word as well
the two letters go into separate parts of the school word, not side by side

parts.note: a college is a school

explanation.surface: A colleague from a university works in another part of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different parts of' means the two letters are not inserted side by side: one goes before the G of the school word and one after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a professional associate, someone you work with.

clue.text: A soft, dainty stomach

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
petite means small and dainty

explanation.surface: Someone with a delicate, dainty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' is a noun disguised: it means a liking for, as in having the stomach for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach can mean desire or relish, which is an appetite.

clue.text: Community coin with almost opulent character

parts.note: EC is short for the European Community
a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for opulent is dropped

parts.note: opulent means rich

explanation.surface: A community currency is described as having a rather rich character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from RICH, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A character, in the sense of an odd or unusual person, is an eccentric.

clue.text: With attachment in motor I steer, I had energy and waste gas

parts.note: a motor is a car
a bond is an attachment or tie
taken as written
a steer is a young ox
I had shortens to I'd
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A driver in a car with an attachment, steering, had energy and exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'in' only link here; the pieces simply run on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide is the gas exhaled as a waste product and given off by engines.

clue.text: Plant keeping forty-one in work

indicators.note: the word for work keeps the number inside it, holding it like a container

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
XLI is 41 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A plant takes forty-one years of work to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads at first as a verb, but it is the definition; the Roman numeral sits inside the abbreviation for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a woodland flowering plant, a relative of the primrose and cowslip.

clue.text: Fit for a cold run?

parts.note: a 'cold run' is a snowy downhill slope, so being fit for one means the snow can be skied on, not a chilly jog

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are fit enough for a run in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' suggests physical fitness and 'run' a jog; here it means suitable, and the run is a ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow or a slope in a state suitable for skiing is described this way.

clue.text: Old habit broken in a way that admits intention

indicators.note: a thing that admits something lets it in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: rent means torn or broken
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: An old habit is broken in a way that lets in a new purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a custom but means clothing, as a monk's habit. 'in a way' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing, and habit can mean dress or attire.

clue.text: Pirates' treasure? They could give peep at it!

definitions.text: Pirates' treasure? They could give peep at it!

parts.words: Pirates' treasure? They could give peep at it!
parts.note: the Spanish coins of pirate lore, read also as bits of the figure 8 on a digital display, whose segments lit separately form letters like P, E, A, I and t

explanation.surface: Pirates gloat over their hoard of coins, letting someone peek at it.
explanation.walkthrough: On a seven-segment display the numeral 8 lights every segment; parts of it make the letters of 'peep at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Spanish silver dollar worth eight reales is the classic pirate coin.

clue.text: Rider's expert view

definitions.note: read as rider is: a rider is an added clause or condition

parts.note: a pro is an expert
vision means view or sight

explanation.surface: A horse rider gives an expert opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a jockey; it is a clause added to a contract, and the 's is short for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a condition attached to an agreement, like a proviso or stipulation.

clue.text: With Queen's Bench individually excluded, is dispute open to debate?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: each letter is left out on its own, not as one block, so they come from separate places

parts.note: a squabble is a dispute
Q is the abbreviation for queen
B stands for bench, as in Queen's Bench, QB

explanation.surface: With the Queen's Bench court out of it, is the dispute still debatable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'individually excluded' takes Q and one B out of SQUABBLE, leaving SUABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an issuable plea or point is one that can be made the subject of an issue, so disputable.

clue.text: Chess win was stifling in relationship?

parts.note: stifling someone is smothering them, here in the past
a mate is a partner in a relationship

explanation.surface: A partner felt suffocated in a relationship, like a game lost at chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' does double service in sense: a partner, and the chess term that ends the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A smothered mate is checkmate by a knight against a king hemmed in by its own pieces.

clue.text: Cultivated particular country dance

parts.note: to hoe soil is to cultivate it
own means particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A specially cultivated dance from a particular country.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance, a type of country dance.

clue.text: Essayist one's introduced to affixes

indicators.note: introduced to means put into the word for affixes

parts.note: affixes means adds on
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: An essayist is introduced to the art of affixes.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into ADDS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an English essayist, co-founder of The Spectator.

clue.text: Rather eco-friendly production of energy

indicators.note: production of means the letters are made into something new, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Producing energy can be rather environmentally friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges ENERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeny means somewhat green, and green means environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Imperfect arrangement for tertiary education?

parts.note: uni, short for university, is tertiary education
a deal is an arrangement or agreement

explanation.surface: An arrangement for university study turns out to be far from perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just joins the pieces; the clue gives DEAL first but the answer puts UNI first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not ideal falls short of perfection, so it is imperfect.

clue.text: Senior sort led astray

indicators.note: letters led astray wander from their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person of some sort is led off the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges SORTLED.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an informal word for an older person, a senior citizen.

clue.text: Some upright stalwarts search thoroughly

indicators.note: in a down clue, upright means the letters are read standing on end, bottom to top
some of the word means a part is taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Some loyal stalwarts search everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes LWART from stalwarts; 'upright' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to search through thoroughly, as a net sweeps the sea.

clue.text: Librettist for Otello getting vocal disapproval about it

indicators.note: the jeer goes about, or around, the other word

parts.note: a boo is a shout of disapproval
taken as written

explanation.surface: The writer of an opera's words is booed by the audience over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Otello is Verdi's opera; the surface suggests the librettist is jeered, which happens to be the wordplay too.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrigo Boito wrote the libretto for Verdi's opera Otello.

clue.text: Orderly delivers hard copy

parts.note: a firm that ships goods delivers them
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly delivers a hard copy of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, tidy as on a well-kept ship.

clue.text: Weather pattern disseminated online

indicators.note: disseminated means spread about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather pattern is spread far and wide on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disseminated' rearranges ONLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: El Nino is a recurring warming of the Pacific that shifts weather worldwide.

clue.text: Doghouse was located without a US engineer

parts.note: a kennel is a doghouse

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: lay is the past of lie, to be located

explanation.surface: Someone in the doghouse was found without a US engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes A from LAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Kennelly was an American electrical engineer, known for the Kennelly-Heaviside layer.
